title: Regional Failover Automation Upgrade — Kickoff Notes (Working Doc)
content:
Doc: working notes from kickoff. Expect edits.

Meeting
- Title: Regional Failover Automation Upgrade kickoff
- Date/time: 2026-01-08 10:00–11:00 PT
- Organizer: Talia Benson
- Notes: Rafael Mendes

Attendees
- SRE / Reliability
  - Sean Gallagher (Reliability program lead)
  - Rafael Mendes (SRE delivery lead)
  - Miles Thornton (failover architecture)
  - Tomáš Novák (runbooks/paging hygiene) — partial
- Routing / Policy
  - Mina Haddad (Routing EM)
  - Ravi Menon (Routing policy TL)
  - Jordan Lee (Policy engine owner)
- Control plane / Platform
  - Ethan Park (Control plane EM)
  - Benji Okafor (rollout/guardrails)
- Infra / Network / Capacity
  - Victor Alvarez (Network reachability)
  - Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet/capacity)
  - Keiko Yamamoto (autoscaling/guardrails) — partial
- Observability / Tooling
  - Allison Grant (Observability lead)
  - Devon Price (incident-bot/tooling)
- Product / Customer
  - Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API product)
  - Lauren Bishop (Dedicated product)
  - Dev Patel (Support escalation owner) — partial
  - Simran Kaur (Private deployments guidance) — partial

Context (why we’re doing this)
- Today: regional failover is a mix of manual actions + partially-automated routing policies.
- Key pain:
  1) triggers are noisy (false positives) and sometimes slow for real regional impairment
  2) hard to safely validate end-to-end behavior (especially across Hosted + Dedicated)
  3) rollback/anti-flap semantics are inconsistent across routes/tiers
  4) during impairment, on-call doesn’t have a single “region is unhealthy” view; too much time spent correlating symptoms
- This project is part of Reliability Program work (SLO maturity, incident reduction, graceful degradation).

Goals (agreed in room)
1) Reduce customer-visible impact during regional impairments
   - shrink detection + decision + traffic shift time
   - prevent cascading overload in “destination” regions
2) Standardize failover trigger hierarchy
   - consistent ordering of signals and required corroboration
   - deterministic policy evaluation (no “it depends who is on call”)
3) Safe automation
   - dry-run mode to compute recommended actions with evidence
   - guardrails: per-tenant and per-route safety limits; approval hooks where needed
   - explicit rollback rules and anti-oscillation
4) Prove it
   - controlled failover tests (game days) with measurable success criteria
   - record outcomes and follow-ups; establish quarterly cadence
5) Better observability
   - dashboards/alerts that let on-call distinguish: region impairment vs. single service vs. capacity exhaustion vs. network reachability

Non-goals / boundaries (captured)
- Not doing multi-cloud migration.
- Not rewriting serving runtime.
- Not changing customer contract/SLA language in this effort (Product/Legal separate track).
- Private deployments: provide recommended patterns + docs; not building bespoke customer-specific automation.

Current state (quick walkthrough)
- Routing policy engine supports some failover via weighted routing and manual flips.
- Signals used today vary by route (some use 5xx, some tail latency, some “region disabled” flags).
- No single source of truth for “region health”; multiple dashboards with different queries.
- During events, on-call often:
  - checks provider status + internal 5xx/latency
  - manually flips policy or disables a region
  - then scrambles to confirm Dedicated pools don’t overload

Proposed high-level design (discussion summary)
- Region Health Aggregator Service
  - consumes: reachability probes, error burn, tail latency burn, capacity/headroom, control-plane availability signals
  - outputs: region health state + confidence + evidence
  - must fail safe (if aggregator is down/partitioned, policy engine behavior must be deterministic and conservative)
- Trigger signal hierarchy (draft; see ADR-042)
  - reachability (authoritative) > 5xx burn > tail latency burn > capacity exhaustion
  - corroboration: do not fail over on a single weak signal unless it’s reachability confirmed by probes from multiple vantage points
  - dampening and hold-down timers to avoid flaps
- Automated controller
  - consumes region health + policy config
  - supports dry-run + execution mode
  - emits audit events for every recommendation and action (why/what/who/when)
- Rollback semantics (ADR-043)
  - explicit conditions + anti-flap
  - per-tenant safety limits (max flips/hour; blast radius constraints)

Risks / concerns raised
- False positives in staging
  - reachability probes can fail due to unrelated networking hiccups; need quorum + multi-vantage + “probe health” metrics
- Oscillation / flapping
  - the worst outcome is repeated policy flips causing thundering herd + cache churn
  - need rate limiting + hold-down timers + rollback gating
- Capacity / overload in destination region
  - failover can move load faster than autoscaling; must integrate headroom thresholds + load shedding
  - Dedicated pools: avoid draining/evacuating in a way that surprises enterprise customers
- Control plane as a dependency
  - if control plane degrades, we may lose visibility or the ability to execute policy changes
  - need a “degraded mode” and runbook on when to stop automation
- Client behavior
  - streaming clients and retry patterns can amplify impact during redirects
  - gateway timeouts/retry budgets must be tuned; consistent retry-after semantics
- Observability cardinality
  - new labels like failover_reason/trigger_source/tenant_tier can explode cardinality if we’re not careful

Open questions (to resolve in design phase)
1) What is the authoritative trigger for a “regional event” vs “partial degradation”?
   - ex: data plane 5xx high but control plane fine; or only a subset of models/pools affected
2) Who/what can initiate automation in production?
   - always require on-call ack initially?
   - conditions for moving to “no-approval” automation
3) How do we define blast radius?
   - per-tenant (top N accounts) vs per-route vs per-model vs per-capacity-tier
4) Dedicated behavior
   - when we fail over Hosted, how do we ensure Dedicated doesn’t lose headroom?
   - do we gate Hosted failover on Dedicated headroom for shared infra regions?
5) Rollback behavior
   - is rollback automatic once signals recover, or do we require a steady-state window?
   - how do we avoid “rollback too early” when the impaired region is still unstable?
6) Data residency / security boundaries
   - which enterprise tiers/routes are pinned to regions and must not fail over cross-region?
   - how do we enforce in policy config (denylist/constraints)
7) Test strategy
   - minimal blast radius for production game day (which tenants, which routes/models)
   - what do we tell Support/CS ahead of time, and what do we publish (if anything)

Baseline metrics + dashboards (links to fill / verify)
NOTE: Links are placeholders; Allison/Sergio to confirm canonical dashboards.
- Multi-region availability (Hosted API): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/hosted-multi-region-availability
- Multi-region availability (Dedicated): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/dedicated-multi-region-availability
- Routing policy flips / change events: https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/routing-policy-events
- Region reachability probes (perf-canary): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/perf-canary-cross-region
- API gateway error rate + latency burn: https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/api-gateway-slo
- Capacity/headroom by region: https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/fleet-headroom-by-region
- Incident timeline tool (internal): https://incidents.redwoodinference.net/

Recent incidents / motivating examples (to confirm IDs)
- 2025-11: us-east partial impairment (elevated 5xx + timeouts); manual routing changes; detection slow due to noisy canary
- 2025-12: control plane elevated latency leading to delayed policy updates; confusion on whether to fail over
- 2026-01 (staging): failover controller crash on missing signal stream (NPE) during rehearsal; highlighted need for “missing signal” defaults + regression tests

Decisions / agreements from kickoff
- We will ship dry-run mode before enabling any production execution.
- We will define and document a single trigger hierarchy and require deterministic evaluation.
- Every automation action must emit an audit event with evidence signals and links to dashboards.
- Game days are first-class deliverables; success criteria must include both customer impact and operational clarity (on-call experience).

Immediate next steps (next 7–10 days)
- Miles + Ravi: draft ADR-042 initial signal hierarchy with explicit corroboration + timers; circulate for architecture review.
- Rafael + Benji: propose guardrails (rate limits, per-tenant constraints, approvals) and tie to ADR-043.
- Allison + Sergio: baseline dashboards list (canonical links) + gaps list (what panels/metrics missing for game day).
- Victor: define reachability probe quorum rules + vantage points; identify known provider behaviors that can create false positives.
- Vanessa: provide headroom thresholds by region for “safe to fail over” and what metrics are reliable during incidents.
- Devon: incident-bot plan for summarizing failover events + linking to dashboards.
- Talia: compile RACI draft + comms plan skeleton for planned test window.

Action items (with owners)
- [Miles] Outline region health states + state transitions (Healthy/Degraded/Unhealthy/Unknown) and what each means for routing.
- [Ravi/Jordan] Confirm policy engine deterministic evaluation semantics (tie-breakers, missing signal defaults, caching TTL expectations).
- [Ethan] Identify control plane failure modes that block failover execution; propose fallback/escape hatch.
- [Peter] Review gateway retry/timeout budget requirements for cross-region redirects and overload (retry-after standardization).
- [Tomáš] Start runbook delta list: what changes with automation, approvals, rollback, and Dedicated drain coordination.
- [Simran] List private deployment constraints and “supported vs recommended” failover guidance to keep us from overpromising.

Milestones (strawman)
- Week 1–2: baseline + requirements; finalize SLO targets and what counts as regional event
- Week 3–4: ADRs (signal hierarchy, rollback semantics) and test plan draft
- Week 5–8: build (region health service, controller, capacity + reachability integration, dashboards/alerts)
- Week 9–10: staging drills; dry-run in prod behind feature flag
- Week 11–12: controlled production failover test with explicit go/no-go and rollback criteria

Parking lot (captured but not discussed)
- How to communicate “planned test” vs “real incident” in Console banner/status widget.
- Whether we need per-model failover vs per-route failover (e.g., some models only available in some regions).
- What to do about long-lived streaming connections during failover (client guidance + server behavior).

Appendix: quick pointer list (for new folks)
- Umbrella tracking: Linear ENG-2411 (Regional Failover Automation Upgrade)
- ADRs: ADR-042 (signal hierarchy), ADR-043 (rollback semantics)
- SLO doc: Multi-region availability SLO 2026 (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Game day: initial plan will be us-east → eu-west with limited tenants/models + tight blast radius
